# HTML PPT · GitHub 暗紫渐变

A focused entry point into the [`html-ppt`](../html-ppt/SKILL.md) master skill that lands the user directly on the **`obsidian-claude-gradient`** full-deck template.

## When this card is picked

The Examples gallery wires "Use this prompt" to the example_prompt above. When you accept that prompt, this card is the right pick if the user wants exactly the visual identity of `obsidian-claude-gradient` (see the upstream [full-decks catalog](../html-ppt/references/full-decks.md) for screenshots and rationale).

## How to author the deck

1. **Read the master skill first.** All authoring rules live in
   [`skills/html-ppt/SKILL.md`](../html-ppt/SKILL.md) — content/audience checklist,
   token rules, layout reuse, presenter mode, the keyboard runtime, and the
   "never put presenter-only text on the slide" rule.
2. **Start from the matching template folder:**
   `skills/html-ppt/templates/full-decks/obsidian-claude-gradient/` — copy `index.html` and
   `style.css` into the project, keep the `.tpl-obsidian-claude-gradient` body class.
3. **Bring the shared runtime with the template.** The upstream
   `index.html` links the shared CSS/JS via `../../../assets/...` because it
   sits three folders deep inside `skills/html-ppt/templates/full-decks/`.
   Once you copy `index.html` into the project, those parent-relative URLs
   no longer resolve and `base.css`, `animations.css`, and `runtime.js`
   will 404 — meaning the deck never activates and slide navigation is
   dead. Pick one of these two recipes per project:
   - **Recipe A — copy + rewrite (preferred):** copy
     `skills/html-ppt/assets/fonts.css`, `skills/html-ppt/assets/base.css`,
     `skills/html-ppt/assets/animations/animations.css`, and
     `skills/html-ppt/assets/runtime.js` into a project-local
     `assets/` (with `assets/animations/animations.css`), then rewrite the
     four `<link>`/`<script>` tags in `index.html` from
     `../../../assets/...` to the matching project-local paths
     (`assets/fonts.css`, `assets/base.css`,
     `assets/animations/animations.css`, `assets/runtime.js`).
   - **Recipe B — inline:** read the same four files and replace each
     `<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../../assets/...">` with a
     `<style>...</style>` containing the file's contents, and the
     `<script src="../../../assets/runtime.js">` with a
     `<script>...</script>` containing `runtime.js`. Yields a single
     self-contained `index.html`.
   Either way, do not ship the upstream `../../../assets/...` URLs
   verbatim into a project artifact — they only work in-tree.
4. **Pick a theme.** Default tokens look fine; if the user wants a different
   feel, swap in any of the 36 themes from `skills/html-ppt/assets/themes/*.css`
   via `<link id="theme-link">` and let `T` cycle.
5. **Replace demo content, not classes.** The `.tpl-obsidian-claude-gradient` scoped CSS only
   recognises the structural classes shipped in the template — keep them.
6. **Speaker notes go inside `<aside class="notes">` or `<div class="notes">`** — never as visible text on the slide.

## Attribution

Visual system, layouts, themes and the runtime keyboard model come from
the upstream MIT-licensed [`lewislulu/html-ppt-skill`](https://github.com/lewislulu/html-ppt-skill). The
LICENSE file ships at `skills/html-ppt/LICENSE`; please keep it in place when
redistributing.

Open Design
Design, back on your desktop

An open-source, local, agent-driven design platform.
From idea to prototypes, websites, slides, and HTML video —
the entire product design workflow, on your own machine.

📜 Apache-2.0 🖥️ Runs locally 🔑 BYOK · No sign-up
02 / 08
● CHAPTER 01

Why open?

In April 2026, Claude Design proved for the first time that LLMs can truly design.
But it is closed-source, paid, and cloud-only — Open Design sets that capability free.

03 / 08
● COMPARE

Closed cloud tools vs Open Design · Who serves creators

CLOSED CLOUD TOOLS

Powerful, but locked down

They proved LLMs can design, but —
• Locked to one model vendor; no swapping agents
• Cloud-only; no self-hosting, no BYOK
• Closed-source and paid — the capability is never yours

OPEN DESIGN

Desktop-native + agent-ready

Built for creators from day one —
• Reads local files, Figma exports, and code repos directly
• Claude Code / Codex / Cursor plug in out of the box
• Apache-2.0: fork it, self-host it, ship it commercially

💡 Key insight: put frontier AI design capability back on every creator's desk.
04 / 08
● WORKFLOW · 4 STEPS

From idea to delivery, one workflow

1

Pick a starting point

Describe your goal in one sentence, or start straight from a template or plugin.

2

Lock the visual direction

Once a direction is chosen, palette, type, and spacing flow into generation automatically.

3

Generate artifacts

The agent reads the full context and produces real, runnable files — preview and edit instantly in the sandbox.

4

Ship, or turn it into video — memory compounds

Hand off to engineering, or convert to a marketing video with HyperFrames; every choice becomes context for the next generation.

05 / 08
● LOCAL DATA

Your data stays on your machine

// .od/ — all of Open Design's runtime data lives in this local directory
.od/
├── app.sqlite          // local SQLite: sessions & design memory
├── projects/           // per-project agent working directories
├── artifacts/          // generated prototypes / slides / videos
└── media-config.json   // BYOK credentials, API keys never leave the machine

No sign-up, no cloud sync — git it, diff it, roll it back. Design artifacts are finally version-controlled.
